deployment.commit_message:
GAP-FILL: patch_mode's existing-content ceiling blocked any target file over 200KB; queue V4 Overlay Action mission

HAND-AUTHORED-JUSTIFICATION for routes/factory-mount-routes.js: narrow
correctness fix, no new module. Live-reproduced twice: CV1P-S03's patch-mode
dispatch against public/overlay/lifeos-app.html (234KB) returned near-empty
output (90 bytes, then 480 bytes) with no syntax/import error -- meaning the
model wasn't failing to generate valid content, it was failing to find
anything to patch. Traced the actual prompt construction: PATCH MODE's own
instructions tell the model to copy its OLD block "verbatim from EXISTING
FILE CONTENT below", but that section is gated by
shouldIncludeExistingFileContent(), which used the same 200KB ceiling
(MAX_EXISTING_CONTENT_BYTES) as full-file regeneration -- so for anything over
200KB, the model was told to copy from a section that was never actually
included in its prompt. This is a real prompt-construction gap, not a codegen
quality issue, and it made patch_mode -- the feature specifically built
tonight to handle large files safely -- silently unusable for the largest
files that need it most. Gave patch_mode its own, much higher ceiling (2MB)
since its output size doesn't scale with input size the way full-file
regeneration does; full-file regeneration's own 200KB ceiling is unchanged.

BLUEPRINT/FOUNDER_PACKET/BP_PRIORITY/package.json changes are blueprint/spec
text only (SO-001 carve-out). V4 Overlay Action mission scaffolded following
the same minimal-real-requirements path proven for V1/V2/V3 tonight. Ports the
already-proven prototype scripts/prototype-overlay-action-v4.mjs (10/10
tests), parse/approve/execute logic only -- browser session management
(launching Puppeteer) is explicitly out of scope per the founder packet, since
services/browser-agent.js already exists for that.
